title: The genus is invariant under base change
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $K/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] and $X$ a smooth projective curve over $k$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] which is geometrically irreducible over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] and has $H^0(X,\mathcal{O}_X)=k$. Let $X_K=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ be the base change [def-pc-base-change], a scheme over $K$, with structure sheaf $\mathcal{O}_{X_K}$, and let $H^1(-,-)$ be sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology], so that $H^1(X_K,\mathcal{O}_{X_K})$ is a $K$-vector space and $H^1(X,\mathcal{O}_X)$ a $k$-vector space. Then $H^1(X_K,\mathcal{O}_{X_K})$ is finite-dimensional over $K$ and $$\dim_KH^1(X_K,\mathcal{O}_{X_K})=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal{O}_X)=g(X),$$ the genus of $X$ [def-pc-genus] ([def-weil-vector-space-dimension]). Consequently $g(X_K)=g(X)$ for every genus of $X_K$ that is defined as $\dim_KH^1(X_K,\mathcal{O}_{X_K})$: (a) when $X_K$ is a smooth projective curve over $K$ which is geometrically irreducible over $K$, for its genus $g(X_K)$ of [def-pc-genus]; (b) when $K$ is algebraically closed and $X_K$ is a proper smooth connected curve over $K$ in the sense of [def-sc-curves], for its genus $g(X_K)$ of [def-sc-genus].

proof.text: The structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper: $X$ is a smooth projective curve over $k$, and a smooth projective curve over a field is proper over it [lem-pc-projective-proper].

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence: 'and the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec} k$ is proper'

proof.text: $K$ is a flat $k$-algebra: as a $k$-vector space $K$ has a basis, so it is a free $k$-module, and a free module is flat (a direct sum of copies of $k$, and $-\otimes_k k^{(I)}=(-)^{(I)}$ preserves injections).

By [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent], applied to the proper $k$-scheme $X$ (step 1), the flat $k$-algebra $k'=K$ (step 2), the quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ and $i=1$, we get an isomorphism of $K$-vector spaces $H^1(X_K,(\mathcal O_X)_K)\cong H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)\otimes_kK$, where $(\mathcal O_X)_K=p^*\mathcal O_X$ is the pullback [def-pc-base-change] along the projection $p:X_K\to X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf], applied to $g=p$, the canonical map $p^*\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_{X_K}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X_K}$-modules, hence induces a $K$-linear isomorphism on $H^1$ ($H^1$ is a functor [pqf-def-cohomology], and the $K$-structures on both sides come from $\mathcal O_{X_K}$). So $H^1(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})\cong H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)\otimes_kK\cong K\otimes_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ as $K$-vector spaces, the last map being the swap $v\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes v$.

$V=H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space by [lem-pc-genus-well-defined] ($X$ is a geometrically irreducible smooth projective curve over $k$), and $\dim_kV=g(X)$ by [def-pc-genus]. By [lem-pc-finrank-field-base-change], $K\otimes_kV$ is finite-dimensional over $K$ with $\dim_K(K\otimes_kV)=\dim_kV$. With step 3, $H^1(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})$ is finite-dimensional over $K$ and $\dim_KH^1(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)=g(X)$ ([def-weil-vector-space-dimension]: isomorphic vector spaces have equal dimension).

The two consequences are instances of the definitions: in case (a) [def-pc-genus] applied over the field $K$ to $X_K$ gives $g(X_K)=\dim_KH^1(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})$, and in case (b) [def-sc-genus] applied to the proper smooth connected curve $X_K$ over the algebraically closed field $K$ ([def-sc-curves]) gives the same; by step 4 this is $g(X)$.

source.place: statement: '$g(X_K)=\dim_KH^1(X_K,\mathcal{O}_{X_K})$' and 'this applies in particular when $X_K$ is a connected curve in the sense of [def-sc-curves]'
